title: Camp 4 close: the thirtieth part
hook: the part every Muslim child knows is now yours too

segments.voice: Yesterday, ma'a: with hardship, ease, or whichever line pulled at you. Your line was one verse, kept.

Somewhere right now, a seven-year-old is sitting cross-legged on a mosque carpet, rocking slightly, reciting Qul a'udhu bi rabbin-nas for the hundredth time while a teacher listens with one ear and corrects with one finger. Tomorrow it'll be the next surah. In a few years, the whole last part. It's the same in Karachi, Lagos, Istanbul, Detroit. The children don't start with the long surahs at the front of the book. They start at the end, with the short ones, and work backward. That's exactly what you've done for seventy-five days. Today this camp closes.
screen: `A CHILD ON A MOSQUE CARPET.` → `STARTING FROM THE END.` → `SEVENTY-FIVE DAYS, THE SAME ROAD.`

segments.voice: Look back at the road. You began by hearing before reading: tilawah, the Qur'an as something recited aloud before it was ever a book on a shelf. Then ta'awwudh, taking refuge before you begin. Then An-Nas, the whisperer who withdraws, and from there backward, surah by surah. Al-Ikhlas and the One, ahad. Al-Kawthar's abundance. Al-Ma'un's small kindnesses. By time, people are in loss. The earth telling its news. Al-Qadr, peace until dawn. Read, the first word ever revealed. With hardship, ease. The orphan, again and again. The soul at peace, returning. Al-Wadud, the Loving. The buried girl who will be asked. The man who frowned, and was corrected. Until An-Naba', the great news, where the juz' begins. Then you carried it: into prayer, into sleep with Ayat al-Kursi, into the Fatiha heard fresh, into tajwid and zayyinu, into one verse, kept. Bukhari records the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ saying: the best of you are those who learn the Qur'an and teach it. That's why the seven-year-old is on the carpet, and why a grandparent somewhere is listening. The juz' isn't the whole Qur'an. It's the doorway most people walk through. Now the path goes further in. Camp five has four strands: the most beautiful names of Allah, the Prophet's life in Medina, Rumi and the Sufi path for those who choose it, and how the Qur'an itself is built. Tomorrow begins with the names.
screen: `HEARING, THEN REFUGE.` · `FROM AN-NAS BACK TO AN-NABA'.` · `CARRIED INTO PRAYER, SLEEP AND VOICE.` · `THE DOORWAY MOST PEOPLE WALK THROUGH.` · then, large: `THE ONES EVERY CHILD KNOWS.`

segments.voice: Sit the way that child sits, if your body lets you, and choose one surah you know by heart, or nearly: al-Ikhlas is four lines, the Fatiha seven, and if you don't have a whole one yet, take the verse you kept yesterday. Recite it from memory, without looking, slowly, in Arabic or in English, and if you stumble, remember the two rewards and keep going. When you finish, sit in the quiet: this is in you now.
Hifz, keeping and memorizing: seventy-five days through the thirtieth part, from An-Nas back to An-Naba', the surahs every Muslim child learns first.
Your line: the ones every child knows. Now they're yours too. Camp four, complete.

howItsDone: Muslim children usually memorize Juz' 'Amma first, from An-Nas backward, with a teacher at a mosque, a weekend school or at home; in many families finishing it is marked with a small celebration.

guess: copying the Qur'an out by hand

fork.setup: the Prophet names who is best among you. who?
options: those who learn the Qur'an and teach it
those who read the most pages
fork.reveal: Bukhari: the best of you are those who learn the Qur'an and teach it. the child and the teacher both count.

original.note: Arabic: keeping, memorizing. one who memorizes the whole Qur'an is a hafiz.

trapdoor: what you thought: the last and least important part of the Qur'an.
what it means: the part learned first, recited most, and carried into prayer, sleep and daily life.
what a scholar hears: hifz from h-f-z, to guard; Bukhari 5027, the best learn and teach; most of the juz' is Meccan and early.
